article_title: What can I do if I did not receive my order?
summary: Explains how customers can report an order that did not arrive through DoorDash account help, mobile app, or desktop. The article says DoorDash investigates reports of orders not delivered and routes users through prompts to select a resolution or chat with an agent.
user_action_required: Report the issue from Orders > Help > Delivery Issues > Order never arrived, then follow prompts to select a resolution or chat with an agent.
policy_conditions: DoorDash states it investigates every reported never-delivered order, but does not publish explicit refund eligibility rules on this page.
refund_or_credit_language: The article mentions selecting a resolution, chatting with an agent, and contacting live support. It also includes chat and phone support options.
escalation_path: Yes. Resolution depends on the specific order and DoorDash review.
evidence_type: The answer depends on an app/account flow after selecting the specific order. Public article provides reporting steps but not final eligibility logic.
source_dependency_notes: No visible last-updated date observed; article shows 2 min read.

article_title: I would like to get a refund on the trip I didn't take
summary: Provides a help flow for riders who did not take a requested trip but were charged. The page asks the rider to select the date or toggle below and says Uber will get back to them. It also links to Uber's refund policy and requires login for help.
user_action_required: Select the relevant date or toggle on the help page, log in, and submit the issue to Uber.
policy_conditions: The page indicates the rider can report a charged trip they did not take, but does not state the decision rules for refund approval on the page itself.
refund_or_credit_language: The page says Uber will get back to the rider and links to the refund policy.
escalation_path: Yes. The rider must log in and submit details about the specific trip.
evidence_type: This page is relevant to full-trip charges for trips the rider says they did not take. It may not cover cancellation fees or temporary authorization holds by itself.

summary: Explains when riders may be charged cancellation fees, when cancellation fees do not apply, how cancellation fees vary, how authorization holds can look like charges, and how riders can request review if they believe they were incorrectly charged.
user_action_required: Review whether the charge was a cancellation fee, full fare, or authorization hold. If the rider believes the cancellation fee was incorrect, enter the trip date or complete the linked form for a ride they did not take.
policy_conditions: Cancellation fee timing is stated by ride type. The article says a cancellation fee will not apply if Uber detects the driver has not made progress to the pickup location or if the driver is 5 or more minutes late. It also explains that GPS-based arrival time may not perfectly match real-world coordinates.
refund_or_credit_language: The article does not guarantee a refund, but says riders can submit details if they believe they were incorrectly charged and Uber will get back to them.
escalation_path: The page routes users to enter the date for an incorrect cancellation fee or complete the linked form if they did not take the trip.
account_specific_dependency: Yes. Final review depends on trip date, ride type, driver progress, driver arrival/wait time, cancellation reason, GPS-derived pickup arrival, and charge type.
source_dependency_notes: This article is relevant if the charge was a cancellation fee. The broader user question may also require the trip-not-taken refund page or authorization hold explanation depending on what kind of charge the rider sees.
staleness_notes: No visible last-updated date observed. Article notes Uber periodically experiments with cancellation policy changes, increasing freshness risk.

article_title: Cancel and no-show fee policy for drivers
summary: Driver-facing article explaining when drivers are paid cancellation or no-show fees. It includes conditions such as whether the passenger's cancellation window passed and whether the driver was still on track to arrive by the original ETA.
user_action_required: Not applicable to rider directly. This article is for drivers and explains driver compensation conditions.
policy_conditions: Drivers may be paid cancellation fees when rider cancellation or no-show conditions are met. For rate card regions, driver payment can depend on time and distance driven. Drivers may not be paid if they are too far from pickup or miss required no-show steps.
refund_or_credit_language: Does not explain rider refunds. It explains driver payment eligibility.
escalation_path: No direct rider escalation path. Driver-facing help content only.
account_specific_dependency: Yes. Driver payout depends on ride status, ETA, driver location, and whether no-show/cancel steps were completed.
source_dependency_notes: This article was the top Lyft Help search result for a rider question, but it is the wrong audience. It may confuse a customer or an AI system if retrieved without audience filtering.

article_title: Cancel and no-show policy for riders
summary: Rider-facing article explaining pending charges, cancellation fees, no-show fees, and how to dispute a fee. It says riders may be charged a cancellation fee in certain situations and can dispute wrongly charged cancel or no-show fees in the app.
user_action_required: If the rider thinks the fee was wrong, open the Lyft app, go to profile > Account > Ride history, select the ride, and choose Dispute ride charge.
policy_conditions: Riders may be charged a cancellation fee if they cancel more than 30 seconds after a driver accepts, more than 30 seconds after requesting Wait and Save, after the driver arrives, or after 3 or more rides in a 15-minute timeframe. No-show fees may apply when the driver arrived, waited the required time, and attempted contact.
refund_or_credit_language: The article does not guarantee a refund. It says riders can dispute a wrongly charged cancel or no-show fee.
escalation_path: The article provides an in-app dispute path through Ride history > Dispute ride charge.
account_specific_dependency: Yes. Final outcome depends on the ride, cancellation timing, driver arrival/progress, whether the charge was pending, and Lyft's review.
source_dependency_notes: Correct rider-facing article. The exact user scenario about the driver 'not moving' is not directly addressed as an exception, so an agent should route the user to dispute rather than promise a refund.

summary: Explains refund and return policy for grocery and other retailer orders. Customers can self-report order problems within 3 days of pickup or delivery, excluding restaurant orders, for a credit or refund. Missing or damaged items may be eligible for refund or credit up to the amount paid.
user_action_required: Self-report order problems within 3 days of pickup or delivery. For missing items, report items that were charged on the final receipt but not received.
policy_conditions: Missing items must be reported within 3 days of pickup or delivery. Missing items must have been charged on the final receipt. Refunds are subject to certain conditions. High-value or certified delivery items may require in-store return depending on retailer policy.
refund_or_credit_language: Instacart can issue a refund or credit toward a future order up to the amount paid for an item. Partial refund or credit may apply if only part of an item is missing or damaged. Instacart processes refunds immediately, though payment method or bank timing may vary.
escalation_path: For assistance, customers can contact Customer Experience by selecting Get Help. EBT SNAP and OTC/Medicare card refunds require contacting Instacart Customer Experience rather than the retailer.
account_specific_dependency: Yes. Eligibility may depend on item, receipt, payment method, retailer policy, timing, and whether the order is grocery/retailer vs. restaurant.
source_dependency_notes: This article gives refund/credit policy. It should be paired with the order-problem reporting article for step-by-step customer action.

article_title: Report a problem with your order
summary: Explains how to report order issues such as missing items, incorrect items, damaged or spoiled items, poor replacements, late orders, wrong order delivered, and orders that never arrived. Provides app and website steps.
user_action_required: In the app, go to Account > Orders > Get help on the relevant order, choose the issue, select affected items, and select a preferred resolution. On the website, go to Your orders, click Report a problem, select the issue and affected items, then select a preferred resolution.
policy_conditions: Order issues must be self-reported within 3 days of pickup or delivery. Not all issues automatically qualify for a credit or refund. EBT SNAP orders are not eligible for credit and require refund handling through Instacart Customer Experience.
refund_or_credit_language: Instacart can issue a credit or refund for eligible issues. Refund or credit may be up to the amount paid; partial refund or credit may apply. Same-day refund may be possible if reported within 24 hours. Credits appear in Credits, promos & gift cards and apply automatically at checkout.
escalation_path: The article says to log in for help and includes a Customer Experience path for some refund types such as EBT SNAP, OTC/Medicare, PayPal, or Klarna issues.
account_specific_dependency: Yes. Final resolution depends on order issue, affected items, timing, payment method, eligibility, and possibly retailer policy.
source_dependency_notes: This article gives the reporting flow and detailed refund/credit conditions. It is highly relevant to missing grocery items.
